issues.summary: For values of 4 chars or fewer, list shows fewer than value[:4] chars to avoid revealing the full value, a reasonable deviation from the literal spec.
Minor lint findings: raise without 'from', percent formatting, long lines.

issues.evidence: probe p15; `set k abc` then `list` prints 'k  abc***' (B/vault.py:243)
issues.summary: list reveals the entire secret for values of 4 characters or fewer, violating 'never the full value'.
--ttl 0 is accepted and silently stores an already-expired secret.

issues.evidence: B/vault.py:178-185 value is a required positional argument
issues.summary: Secret values can only be passed on argv (visible in process listings); there is no stdin option.

issues.evidence: static/B-ruff.txt C901 run() complexity 17; B904, UP031
issues.summary: Single monolithic run() dispatcher with high complexity plus minor lint findings.

blinding_guess.why: B ships a test suite that maps nearly one-to-one to the numbered requirements (test_exit_code_map, test_kdf_and_salt, etc.), which suggests it was built from a spec.

notes: The probes ran under Python 3.9 with cryptography from the user site (PYTHONUSERBASE passed through) and HOME set to a temporary directory. Probe p15 reads 'never the full value' as overriding the literal value[:4] for short values. That is the only probe that separates A from B. A and B pick different exit codes when VAULT_MASTER_KEY is missing (A gives 1, B gives 2); both are defensible, so neither is penalised. B's own unittest suite ran with unittest because pytest is not installed.
